scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Two clocks disagree
scenes.caption: Aditi and Vihaan inspect invented observation cards in the Decision Lab. The borrowed tablet is documented as seven minutes fast relative to reference. Events use whole minutes since midnight within one stated day.
scenes.speech: Aditi and Vihaan inspect invented observation cards in the Decision Lab. The borrowed tablet is documented as seven minutes fast relative to reference. Events use whole minutes since midnight within one stated day.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The apparent order
scenes.caption: Reference and tablet cards appear reversed when sorted by displayed values. Vihaan almost calls the sequence impossible. Aditi asks whether the numbers share a clock basis before interpreting the order or inventing a cause.
scenes.speech: Reference and tablet cards appear reversed when sorted by displayed values. Vihaan almost calls the sequence impossible. Aditi asks whether the numbers share a clock basis before interpreting the order or inventing a cause.
scenes.dialogue: Different clock bases can mislead an ordering.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Apply the documented correction
scenes.caption: They subtract the documented fast offset from each tablet value and leave reference values unchanged. Corrected cards share the supplied basis. No hidden timezone or daylight-saving rule applies; the example stays within the same day.
scenes.speech: They subtract the documented fast offset from each tablet value and leave reference values unchanged. Corrected cards share the supplied basis. No hidden timezone or daylight-saving rule applies; the example stays within the same day.
scenes.dialogue: A fast clock needs subtraction here.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Observations are not identities
scenes.caption: The normalized sequence describes when observations occurred on that basis. It does not identify who held the tablet or why a page changed. Vihaan puts those guesses in unresolved fields instead of the observation labels.
scenes.speech: The normalized sequence describes when observations occurred on that basis. It does not identify who held the tablet or why a page changed. Vihaan puts those guesses in unresolved fields instead of the observation labels.
scenes.dialogue: A time conversion cannot supply a missing actor.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Build a reproducible timeline
scenes.caption: Aditi places each card by its normalized minute and retains the original displayed value beside it. The teacher can reproduce the calculation from the same offset. Their timeline explains the changed order without claiming that order proves causation.
scenes.speech: Aditi places each card by its normalized minute and retains the original displayed value beside it. The teacher can reproduce the calculation from the same offset. Their timeline explains the changed order without claiming that order proves causation.
scenes.dialogue: Keep original and converted values together.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Leave unknowns visible
scenes.caption: The finished record labels the clock basis, offset and same-day assumption, while actor and cause remain unknown. Your evidence must let another learner repeat the conversion and distinguish chronology from unsupported intention or responsibility claims.
scenes.speech: The finished record labels the clock basis, offset and same-day assumption, while actor and cause remain unknown. Your evidence must let another learner repeat the conversion and distinguish chronology from unsupported intention or responsibility claims.
scenes.dialogue: A cautious timeline can be useful with unknown fields.
